CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K NATARAJAN  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K NATARAJAN)

This petition is filed by accused Nos.1 to 6 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C. No.8050/23 arising out of Crime No.16/2023 of Bidar Women Police Station and charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506, 323 and 149 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
now pending on the file of I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Bidar.

2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:5929 3.
The case of prosecution is that on the complaint of one Saraswati, the wife of petitioner No.1, filed on 18.03.2023, the police registered the FIR.
It is alleged that she married accused No.1 on 15.02.2019 as per their customs and rights.
The said marriage was performed by her father.
At the time of negotiation, the accused persons said to be demanded 20 tolas of gold and the cash of Rs.2 lakhs.
The same was given to accused No.3, prior to the marriage.
After the marriage, the complainant resided in the matrimonial home at Nanded.
She was looked after well for 8 to 9 months.

Thereafter, the accused persons started harassing the complainant stating that the dowry of Rs.2 lakhs given to accused No.1 was very less and another sum of Rs.10 lakhs was required for the purpose of doing business.
There was continuous harassment on the complainant.
Finally, on 17.06.2020, accused Nos.1 to 4 said to be assaulted the complainant.
Accused No.1 brought back the victim to the house of her father and left there, saying that until she brings money, she should not come to the home.
The parents of the NC: 2024:KHC-K:5929 complainant waited for some time.

Then, on 20.01.2023, they called for the meeting of the elders and there was quarrel and the accused persons threatened the well- wishers saying that if they come for any settlement, they will be intimidated.
Hence, the complainant was forced to file the complaint to the police.
Accordingly, the police registered the FIR and investigated the matter and filed charge sheet, which is under challenge.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that there is no specific allegation made against any of the accused persons.
There was delay in lodging the complaint.

Even though on 17.06.2020, there was lockdown period and there was restriction in movement by the intercity passengers, there is no question of the complainant coming to her parents' house brought by accused No 1, is not acceptable.
It is further contended that after more than 21/2 years, the complainant has filed the complaint.

The complainant has falsely implicated the NC:
2024:KHC-K:5929 entire family members of the accused.
Hence, prayed for allowing the petition.
5. Per contra, the learned counsel for respond No.2 has seriously objected the petition contending that there is specific allegation made against all the accused persons.

It is further contended that the complaint about the demand and acceptance of dowry attracts Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and thereafter, demanding the further additional dowry attracts Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
There was continuous harassment on the complainant even including the sisters of accused No.1, i.e. accused Nos.4 and 5.
Therefore, there is material for proceeding against all the accused for trial.
It is contended that accused Nos.4 to 6 have moved application for discharge under Section 239 of Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate and therefore, prayed for dismissing the petition.
Learned High Court Government Pleader has supported the impugned judgment contending that the harassment by the accused persons on the complainant is continuing.
The statement of the parents of the victim and also the statement of the victim corroborates each other.
Therefore, there is a case for trial and prayed for dismissing the petition.
7. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, perused the records.

8. On perusal of the records, on the first part, it is stated that the marriage negotiation was held in the house of the father of the complainant, where all the accused persons discussed and demanded 20 Tolas of gold and Rs.2 lakhs cash as dowry and the same was accepted and the marriage was performed on 15.02.2019.

Subsequently, the parents of accused No.1, including accused No.1,
demanded Rs.10 lakhs for doing the NC: 2024:KHC-K:5929 business by accused No.1 and always assaulted and abused her in filthy language.

9. Accused No.4-Roopali, said to be widow residing in her parents' house, also joined accused No.1,
and was always harassing the complainant.

Accused Nos.5 and 6, though were residing separately,
whenever they come to the house of matrimonial house of complainant, accused No.5-Pranita, said to be instigating accused No.1 and her parents not to leave the complainant and make her to work continuously and she should not take rest.
On 17.06.2020, once again, the family members and others came for settlement and advised the accused, where accused No.1 to 4 said to be assaulted the complainant.
Later, she was brought back to her parents' house, left by accused No.1 stating that she should not come back until she brings money.
Later, another meeting/ panchayath was held on 20.01.2023, where the accused persons demanded money or divorce from the complainant.
Therefore, the complainant forced to file the complaint.

sentences.text: The statement of the parents and relatives clearly reveals that the accused persons are continuously harassing the complainant for dowry.

All the accused persons negotiated and demanded for dowry and therefore, receiving the dowry prior to the marriage attracts Section 3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and the demand for an additional dowry after the marriage attracts Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

The continuous harassment by the accused persons on the complainant, both physically and mentally, attracts Section 498A of IPC.
10.

Though accused No.5 was coming to her parents' house often and instigated the other accused for harassment on the complainant and there were no severe allegations for Section 498A of IPC,
but she was also participated in the marriage negotiation in the demand of dowry prior to the marriage.
Accused No.6, who is the husband of accused No.5, was also participated in demand of dowry prior to the marriage.
Subsequently, he - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5929 came along with his wife and there was continuous harassment on the complainant.
11. Of course, on 17.06.2020, accused No.1 said to be left the complainant-victim in the house of her parents and the complaint was filed only in March 2023.
The final Panchayat was held on 20.01.2023, where all the accused persons said to be demanded dowry or the divorce.
Such being the case, there is specific allegation against all the accused persons for having committed the offence.
Merely, there is no strong evidence of Section 498A of IPC against accused No.4 or 5, but they were party to the marriage negotiation under Section 3 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Such being the case, the case is triable by the Magistrate under Section 220 of the Cr.P.C. and it cannot be bifurcated for conducting proceedings against accused Nos.4 and 5.
Therefore, I am of the view that there is a specific case against all the accused persons for framing of charges and proceeding against them.
Therefore, the petition is devoid of merit and accordingly, it is dismissed.

Sd/-
